comments.content: Tick rows are unbounded but the SVG height and bottom margin are fixed. For tightly clustered breakpoints, row 4 has baseline 344 (partly clipped), row 5 is outside the viewport, and row 3 at 328 can overlap the expiration title at 338. Horizontal scrolling cannot recover content clipped vertically by the SVG. Size the bottom margin/viewBox from the allocated rows (and reserve space for the title), or use a bounded layout that keeps every tick visible. Add a dense-breakpoint layout test.
comments.existing_code: <text key={tick.price.numerator + '/' + tick.price.denominator} x={tick.at} y={HEIGHT - MARGIN.bottom + 16 + tick.row * LINE} textAnchor="middle">

comments.content: The collision registry starts empty and only receives ray, zero-set, and latest-close labels. Tick labels and axis titles never participate, so a zero-set label moved downward can still overlap a tick or title. Also, after six moves the loop accepts the position even if it still collides. This does not guarantee the requested non-overlapping labels. Include all text obstacles in a shared layout pass and provide a collision-free fallback (such as expanding the chart) when no position fits, with tests for coincident annotations.
comments.existing_code: while (placed.some((box) => collides(boxOf(text, x, at, anchor), box)) && Math.abs(at - baseline) < 6 * LINE) at += step;

comments.content: The resolved baseline is not constrained to the SVG viewport. In particular, a latest-close label near a rising ray's endpoint can start just below the ray label and be moved above the top edge: with the ray baseline at 34 and the close baseline at 40, the upward search tries 24 and then accepts 8, clipping the 13px text. This newly introduces clipping even when both original positions were inside the chart. Include viewport bounds in placement and fall back to another direction or expand the chart when upward placement runs out of room.
